intended_object: Given a locally constant f : Spec R → ℕ with N = max f and eᵢ the idempotent of the clopen set {p | i < f p}, the complementary finite projective module Q = ⊕_{i<N} (1 − eᵢ)R. It satisfies P ⊕ Q ≅ Rᴺ, where P = ⊕ᵢ eᵢR realizes f. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and its use in `prodComplementEquiv`.
explanation: The body packages `rankComplement R f`, the product over i : Fin (rankBound f) of Ideal.span {1 - rankIdempotent f i}, as an object of `ModuleCat.FiniteProjective R`. Here rankBound f is the maximum of f's finitely many values, and rankIdempotent f i is the idempotent corresponding to the clopen set {p | i < f p} under Mathlib's `isIdempotentElemEquivClopens`. Each summand is principal, hence finitely generated, and is generated by an idempotent, hence projective; the finite product is therefore finite projective. `prodComplementEquiv` uses this object to give P × Q ≃ R^N componentwise via (e) × (1 − e) ≅ R, so it is exactly the complement the docstring describes. Degenerate cases behave correctly: f ≡ 0 or the zero ring give N = 0 and Q = 0. The setting of a commutative ring is the natural one, since the construction uses Spec R and the idempotent–clopen correspondence. Mathlib has no declaration of this specific module, only its ingredients. The module depends on the choice of bound max f and could be read as an auxiliary construction, but it is a well-defined mathematical object that matches its docstring.
